applicable_when: The kernel uses tl.make_block_ptr with order=(1,0) for B (shape [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K]) then calls tl.trans() to get [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] for tl.dot. Triton implements tl.trans() by staging the tile through shared memory: it writes [BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32] row-major then reads it back column-major, creating stride-BLOCK_N=64 access patterns that cause 7.9-way bank conflicts (64 elements x 4 bytes = 256 bytes = 8 banks hit per warp). The fix is to load B directly in [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] layout by swapping strides in make_block_ptr, so tl.dot receives the tile without any transpose, eliminating the shared memory staging entirely. Additionally, BLOCK_M=128 forces 128x64=8192 FP32 accumulator values driving 168 registers/thread. Reducing BLOCK_M from 128 to 64 halves the accumulator, targeting ~84 registers/thread and enabling 6 blocks/SM (3.2x more occupancy).
